title: GRPO · full NoRA-init with merge/reset
analysis: Completed all 100 steps successfully in 6h43m of training-loop time. Merges at steps 40 and 80 accumulated each learned adapter, created fresh normalized sign A / zero B, and cleared adapter AdamW history while preserving constant LR/scheduler. Backbone synchronization succeeded at startup and both merges. Training correctness over successive 20-step windows was 18.4%, 34.4%, 39.2%, 39.6%, and 37.2%: this run did not sustain renewed improvement after resets. AIME25 avg@8 peaked at 20.0% at step 80, then finished at 15.0% / 30.0% avg@8 / pass@8, versus 17.9% / 36.7% without merges and 20.0% / 43.3% for standard LoRA. These are sampled single-run results on 30 questions. Merge probe max logit differences were 0.25 and 0.3125, with RMS differences 0.0506 and 0.0556; merging was not bitwise function-preserving under mixed-precision forward computation. Peak training allocator usage was 18.00 GiB allocated / 18.96 GiB reserved, including merge work. This explicit Adam-reset baseline does not isolate rank growth from optimizer discontinuity or establish that merging generally fails.

initial-adapter-audit.json.optimizer_reset: clear old adapter Adam state; preserve scheduler and LR
initial-adapter-audit.json.rollout_sync: base W at startup/resume and merges; native adapter BA every step

comparison-audit.json.optimizer_reset: clear adapter moments and step counters at 40 and 80; constant LR and scheduler preserved
comparison-audit.json.rollout_sync: base W then native adapter at startup/resume and after merges; only native adapter between merges
comparison-audit.json.training_allocator_peak_window: policy forward/backward through optimizer, including merge/reset when scheduled
